title: The unemployed builder and the unbuilt house
notes: The two London 1931 stills (6220×8704 portrait) are not crowd pictures: each is an arrest at the 7 October 1931 unemployed demonstration (a man in a cap between two policemen; a young woman held by two policemen). There is no crowd to push into, so each push goes to the face. LABEL-LONDON-1931 rides on each.

Illustrations PH-03-A…E are grey placeholders until Kai approves the Flow plates; LABEL-ILLUSTRATION rides on V4 over every one. 'Picture it small' opens on 03-A (plan), 03-B lands on 'A family needing a house', 03-C on 'The materials'. Then A/B/C hard cuts about 1.6 s each on 'The builder can build. The family needs a home.', and 03-E (the empty plot) held under 'Nothing happens' and 'Need isn't a paying order'.
Verb card follows the storyboard: 1930s · STARVE, on 'That is the second thing you can do. You can starve it.'

What A Life! (1949) shot 12 (176.73–202.13): the close street queue of men in hats (actually a bus queue in the film). Under Keynes's idea only, labelled FROM A 1949 COMEDY; never under the '1930s' lines.

We Work Again (WPA 1937) has no shot log yet; both shots bracketed by grab strips: the Construction Quartermaster hut (≈102.5–112, men striding off to work) and the beam-carrying gang in Harlem (≈187.5–196). Labelled AMERICAN FOOTAGE · 1937.

Considered and not used: BetterHo1935 (Better Housing News Flashes, US 1935) has better builder footage (#10 bricklaying 80.5–82.76, #11 bricklayer close 82.76–84.59, #7 house frames rising) and a falling 1928–34 US residential-construction chart, but we have no LABEL-AMERICAN-FOOTAGE-1935 card; if Kai wants them, render that label and they can replace the WPA shots one for one. gov.archives.arc.13595 (The Plow That Broke the Plains) is not in the conform status and is Dust Bowl, not building.
03-D (the builder at work) lands on 'He's acquired a customer' and carries on into scene 04.
